summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with end-stage liver disease from hepatitis C and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for altered mental status and a first-time generalized tonic-clonic seizure with a focal onset. Initial concerns included infection, metabolic derangements, and intracranial pathology. Workup revealed hyponatremia, markedly elevated blood glucose leading to a new diagnosis of type 1 diabetes, and a urinary tract infection caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae. A non-contrast head CT and MRI showed no acute intracranial abnormality, though EEG indicated diffuse encephalopathy. Lumbar puncture, performed after correction of coagulopathy, ruled out central nervous system infection. The patient improved with antibiotics, insulin, lactulose, and levetiracetam. She was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, resolved infection, and improved mental status, on a regimen including insulin, Keppra, and lactulose, with plans for neurology, endocrinology, and liver follow-up.
